clue.text: Lead English established during tie

indicators.note: something established during another thing is set within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to lash is to tie or bind with rope

explanation.surface: Someone describes a leading English figure confirmed while a match was drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's lead is the strap it is walked on, the same thing as its restraining strap.

clue.text: Using loaf, agree with what smart fellow assumes

parts.note: to loaf about is to lounge idly
to suit is to agree with or be convenient for

explanation.surface: A clever man works out his conclusions by idling and nodding along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assumes' reads as 'supposes', but here it means 'puts on', as clothing; a lounge suit is a man's everyday formal suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartly dressed man puts on this kind of business suit, so it is the outfit he dons.

clue.text: Remains found in forest

definitions.meaning: the residue left after something burns

explanation.definitionFit: Ash is both the powdery residue of a fire and a familiar broadleaved tree of British woods.

clue.text: After Hamlet's entrance, scene for Shakespeare play is set

indicators.note: a word's entrance is its first letter, the way in

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: Theatre talk: once Hamlet has walked on, the set for a Shakespeare production is in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link here; 'set' in the sense of becoming solid is the definition, not stage scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: To set, as concrete or jelly does, is to stiffen and become firm.

clue.text: Drug-taking critic brought to book

parts.note: sounds like a reviewer arrested for narcotics, but describes the essayist who set down his opium habit in a famous book of confessions

explanation.surface: A reviewer who uses drugs is finally punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought to book' means punished, but here literally means put into a book: Thomas De Quincey wrote Confessions of an English Opium-Eater.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas De Quincey was an English essayist and critic whose opium addiction became the subject of his best-known book.

clue.text: Possible loss of merit involved in depression

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed in the hollow word

parts.note: a dent is a small depression in a surface

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of merit are mixed

explanation.surface: An official warns that a dent in morale might cost someone their merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' gives TRIME; 'in' sets it inside the depression, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is harm or damage, the chance of being worse off.

clue.text: Search for eg Holy Grail in Pythonesque style

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the next two words

explanation.surface: A Monty Python film sends knights hunting the Holy Grail in absurd fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A quest is a long search, and the knights' hunt for the Grail is the classic example.

clue.text: Person originally making short list

indicators.note: short means missing its final letter

parts.note: an inventory is a detailed list of items

explanation.surface: Someone first producing a brief list of things.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventor is the person who first devises or makes something new.

clue.text: Couple I saw in a state

parts.note: to couple two things is to connect them
to saw something is to cut it

explanation.surface: Someone reports seeing a pair in some condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of 'see' but is the verb to cut with a saw; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is one of the New England states of the USA.

clue.text: Position taken up with Eastern university

indicators.note: in a down answer, taken up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: the lay of something is its position or arrangement

explanation.surface: An eastern university accepts a post.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut.

clue.text: Girl guide needs these, true to form

indicators.note: the letters are to be formed into something new

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide's handbook requires these items to be done properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl guide' suggests the youth movement, but means a woman who shows people to their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: An usherette is a woman who guides patrons to their seats in a cinema or theatre.

clue.text: Name meat about that can be bought cheaply

indicators.note: one piece goes about, that is around, the other

parts.note: veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A butcher names meat cheap enough to buy.
explanation.definitionFit: A venal person can be bribed, their loyalty purchasable for a small price.

clue.text: Agent with this code to break to finish off assignment

indicators.note: the words are to be broken up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy is given a code to crack to complete the mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: To go the distance is an idiom for lasting to the end and completing a task.

clue.text: Furious about fool producing too much sentimentality

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, around, the second

parts.note: in a tearing rage means furious
a jerk is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about an idiot who is overly sentimental.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear-jerking film is designed to make audiences cry with mawkish emotion.

clue.text: Heading for the bank, go across town

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a bank of keys or seats is a row
to bridge something is to cross it

explanation.surface: Directions: make for the riverbank, then cross into town.
explanation.walkthrough: TROWBRIDGE is the county town of Wiltshire in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Trowbridge is a market town in Wiltshire, England.

clue.text: Major with grumpy expression appearing to have flipped

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: rats is an exclamation of annoyance

explanation.surface: An army major scowls and looks as though he has lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like the military rank but is an adjective; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A star performer is a leading or principal one, as in a star attraction.

clue.text: Toy boy a mum loves to interrupt

indicators.note: the inner letters break into the middle of the outer word

parts.note: Peter is a boy's name
mum means silent, so the call for quiet sh
love is zero in tennis, O, so two loves are OO

explanation.surface: A young lover is interrupted by a mother's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy boy' looks like a phrase for a young lover; 'mum' means keep quiet, not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-shooter is a child's toy tube for blowing dried peas.

clue.text: Pickwickian fellow's upset, one's informed

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a fellow of a college is a don, and with the s gives dons
a grass is someone who has informed on others

explanation.surface: A character from Dickens is upset because someone has told on him.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustus SNODGRASS is a member of the Pickwick Club in Dickens's Pickwick Papers. A grass is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Snodgrass is one of the club members in The Pickwick Papers, so a Pickwickian figure.

clue.text: A French tense's pronunciation that's not learned

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: the word is replaced by one pronounced identically

parts.note: taut means tense or tight

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about a French tense that has not been studied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' suggests grammar but means tight; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untaught has not been learned or acquired through teaching.

clue.text: Order popular with union

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a junction is a joining or union

explanation.surface: A command that goes down well with the trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: An injunction is an authoritative order, especially one from a court.

clue.text: Seconds taken to lower boat

parts.note: a lower is one that lows, or moos, as a cow does

explanation.surface: It takes a few seconds to lower a boat into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as 'let down' but is 'one that lows'; 'taken to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used for carrying cargo.

clue.text: Manage to get to social event

parts.note: to make a place is to reach it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in reaching a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to manage with what is available.

clue.text: Books suggested by university… are important

parts.note: Reading is an English university town
things that matter are important

explanation.surface: Volumes recommended by a university are significant.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading matter is anything to read, such as books.

clue.text: Force rising government leader to be garlanded?

annotationWithheld.why: Force rising government leader to be garlanded? (5): IMPEL is LEI around PM, all reversed, but 'garlanded' must give LEI and also signal the container, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Force rising government leader to be garlanded?

clue.text: Members of church following, long-established

parts.note: old means of long standing

explanation.surface: A congregation follows a longstanding tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold is a flock, so the congregation of a church.

clue.text: Unsettled by alliance of old political group

parts.note: a wing is a faction of a party

explanation.surface: A coalition of an old party is left shaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by alliance of' is link wording joining definition to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is unsettled is still owing, unpaid.

clue.text: Comic pilot Dan Dare's end as a space traveller

indicators.note: comic means funny, so the letters clown about
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Dan Dare, the comic-strip space pilot, finishes as an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare was a British comic hero of the Eagle; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A planetoid is a minor planet or asteroid travelling through space.

clue.text: This individual was successful in audition

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the word is replaced by one sounding identical

parts.note: won means was successful

explanation.surface: An actor succeeded at an audition.
explanation.definitionFit: One means a single individual person.

clue.text: Drug, you have to understand, is taken round country after being cut

indicators.note: the pieces are taken around the next one, enclosing it

parts.note: to dig something is slang for understanding it

indicators.note: cut means losing its last letter

parts.note: Italy is a country

explanation.surface: A drug user is told to grasp that it is smuggled round a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after being cut' drops the country's last letter; 'taken round' has the slang word for understand and 'is' enclose the trimmed country; 'you have to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is a heart drug made from foxglove leaves.

clue.text: Remove front from container to look at plant

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off

parts.note: a box is a container
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Someone takes the lid off a box to see a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a common wild plant.
